ruylopez.e4: Grabs the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop, so White can develop fast and castle early.
ruylopez.e4 e5: Matches White in the centre and frees the f8 bishop, so e4 doesn't control the middle on its own.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3: Develops with a threat to e5, so Black spends the next move defending instead of choosing freely.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6: Guards e5 with a piece rather than ...d6, so the f8 bishop's diagonal stays open and no time is lost.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5: Hits the knight that defends e5. Not a threat yet, but once White castles and plays d4, e5 comes under real pressure.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6: Questions the bishop at once: retreating keeps the tension, while Bxc6 hands Black the bishop pair.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4: Keeps the bishop and the pressure on c6; Black can break the pin with ...b5 whenever needed.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6: Develops and hits e4, so White must decide straight away whether to defend it or castle and let it go.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O: Castles instead of defending e4: if Black takes it, Re1 and d4 win it back with the e-file opened.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 d6: Modern Steinitz: holds e5 with a pawn; with ...a6 in, ...b5 can break the pin whenever it bites.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 b5: Gains queenside space and sends the bishop to b3 early; White can probe the loosened queenside with a4.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6: Exchange Variation: damages Black's pawns for an endgame where White's healthy kingside majority can make a passed pawn.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6: Recaptures towards the centre to open lines for the queen and bishop; the bishop pair offsets the doubled pawns.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6: Berlin Defense: hits e4 at once instead of spending a move on ...a6, forcing White to commit.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O: Castles and lets e4 go: Re1 wins it back while Black's king is still in the centre.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4: Takes the pawn, heading for the Berlin endgame: queens come off early and Black relies on the bishop pair.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 d3: Protects e4 quietly to avoid the Berlin endgame, keeping pieces on for a slow c3 and Nbd2 middlegame.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5: Classical Defense: puts the bishop on its best diagonal, towards f2, before c3 and d4 can blunt it.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 d6: Steinitz Defense: holds e5 with a pawn; solid, but it blocks the f8 bishop and leaves White freer.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5: Schliemann: counterattacks e4 at once to open the f-file before White has finished developing.
ruylopez.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nd4: Bird's Defense: trades off White's knight to ease the pressure on e5, leaving a pawn on d4 that can become a target.

italiangame.e4: Grabs the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop, so White can develop fast and castle early.
italiangame.e4 e5: Matches White in the centre and frees the f8 bishop, so e4 doesn't control the middle on its own.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3: Develops with a threat to e5, so Black spends the next move defending instead of choosing freely.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6: Guards e5 with a piece rather than ...d6, so the f8 bishop's diagonal stays open and no time is lost.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4: Aims at f7, defended only by Black's king, so tactics on f7 shape Black's next few moves.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5: Giuoco Piano: mirrors White, aiming at f2 and taking the bishop's best square before c3 and d4.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3: Prepares d4 to build a big centre, which would also gain time by attacking the c5 bishop.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6: Counterattacks e4 before d4 lands, so if White pushes d4 anyway the centre opens with Black well placed.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d3: Giuoco Pianissimo: keeps the centre closed for a slow build-up with c3, Re1 and Nbd2-f1-g3.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4: Evans Gambit: deflects the bishop with a pawn so c3 and d4 come with tempo.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 O-O: Castles first and keeps c3 and d4 in reserve, choosing the plan after seeing Black's setup.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6: Two Knights: counterattacks e4 rather than copying, accepting that Ng5 can hit f7.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5: Attacks f7 twice. Provocative: the knight has moved twice, so Black gains time if the attack fizzles.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5: Blocks the bishop's diagonal to f7; after exd5 Black usually gives a pawn for fast development.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3: Defends e4 calmly, avoiding the sharp Ng5 and d4 lines for a slow manoeuvring game.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d4: Opens the centre at once, so White can attack while Black's king is still uncastled.
italiangame.e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Be7: Hungarian Defense: a modest bishop that avoids every sharp line, at the cost of a passive position.

kingsgambit.e4: Grabs the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop, so White can develop fast and castle early.
kingsgambit.e4 e5: Matches White in the centre and frees the f8 bishop, so e4 doesn't control the middle on its own.
kingsgambit.e4 e5 f4: Offers the f-pawn to deflect e5, so White can take the centre with d4 and attack down the f-file.
kingsgambit.e4 e5 f4 exf4: Accepts the gambit, usually planning ...g5 to keep the extra pawn and block White's kingside play.
kingsgambit.e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3: Stops ...Qh4+ and supports d4, so White's king stays safe while the centre is built.
kingsgambit.e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5: Defends f4 with another pawn to keep the material, loosening Black's kingside in return.
kingsgambit.e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 h4: Undermines g5 before ...h6 or ...Bg7 can support it, breaking up Black's pawn chain.
kingsgambit.e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 Bc4: Develops at f7, inviting sharp lines after ...g4 where White gives material for the attack.
kingsgambit.e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 d5: Gives the pawn back to strike the centre, so Black develops freely rather than clinging to f4.
kingsgambit.e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 d6: Fischer Defense: covers e5 and g5 first, so ...g5 can follow without knight tricks.
kingsgambit.e4 e5 f4 exf4 Bc4: Bishop's Gambit: allows ...Qh4+, because the king is safe enough on f1 and the queen gets chased.
kingsgambit.e4 e5 f4 d5: Falkbeer Counter-Gambit: strikes the centre instead of taking, punishing the loosened kingside.
kingsgambit.e4 e5 f4 Bc5: Declines: the bishop eyes g1, so White can't castle easily and fxe5 runs into ...Qh4+.

viennagame.e4: Grabs the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop, so White can develop fast and castle early.
viennagame.e4 e5: Matches White in the centre and frees the f8 bishop, so e4 doesn't control the middle on its own.
viennagame.e4 e5 Nc3: Develops and guards e4, keeping the f4 break in reserve as a delayed King's Gambit.
viennagame.e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6: Develops with pressure on e4, so White's f4 ideas come with less force.
viennagame.e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4: Vienna Gambit: strikes at e5, aiming to push e5 and drive the knight from the centre.
viennagame.e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4 d5: Hits back in the centre, opening the position before White's pawns can roll forward.
viennagame.e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4: Aims at f7 while the c3 knight guards e4, ready for sharp play.
viennagame.e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4: A fork trick: takes e4, counting on ...d5 to win the piece back. After Qh5 it gets very sharp.
viennagame.e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 g3: Mieses: a quiet fianchetto, so the bishop controls the long diagonal and d5.
viennagame.e4 e5 Nc3 Nc6: Develops and keeps e5 solid, so f4 meets a well-supported centre.
viennagame.e4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 g3: Fianchettoes for long-term pressure on d5, aiming for slow positional play.
viennagame.e4 e5 Nc3 Bc5: Takes the diagonal towards f2, making the f4 break riskier for White.

queensgambit.d4: Takes the centre with a pawn the queen already guards, so Black can't challenge it at once with ...e5.
queensgambit.d4 d5: Matches White in the centre and stops e4, so White needs c4 to fight for the centre.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4: Offers the c-pawn to lure Black's d-pawn from the centre; if ...dxc4, White regains it later with e3 and Bxc4.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4 e6: Queen's Gambit Declined: holds d5 with a pawn, at the cost of shutting in the c8 bishop for now.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3: Adds pressure on d5, so Black must keep defending it.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6: Guards d5 again while developing, keeping the centre secure.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5: Pins the knight that defends d5, so the pressure builds and Black's development gets awkward.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7: Breaks the pin calmly to castle; Black frees the game later with ...c5 or ...e5.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 cxd5: Exchange Variation: fixes the pawns so White can play b4–b5 against Black's queenside.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3: Natural development that keeps every option, choosing Bg5 or Bf4 later.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5: Tarrasch: accepts an isolated d-pawn for free piece play and open lines.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4 dxc4: Queen's Gambit Accepted: takes, not to keep the pawn but to gain time for ...c5 or ...e5.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4: Builds a full centre while the pawn is away, regaining it later with Bxc4.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3: Develops and stops ...e5, so Black can't free the game before White wins the pawn back.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4 e5: Albin Counter-Gambit: gives a pawn for a cramping pawn on d4 and quick piece play.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4 Nc6: Chigorin: pieces over pawns; the knight hits d4 at once, often with ...Bg4 next.
queensgambit.d4 d5 c4 Bf5: Baltic Defense: gets the light bishop out before ...e6, though Qb3 can then hit b7.

catalan.d4: Takes the centre with a pawn the queen already guards, so Black can't challenge it at once with ...e5.
catalan.d4 Nf6: Develops and stops e4, so White can't build a broad e4–d4 centre without preparing it first.
catalan.d4 Nf6 c4: Gains queenside space and hits d5, so a later ...d5 can be met by exchanging on d5.
catalan.d4 Nf6 c4 e6: Prepares ...d5 or ...Bb4 and opens the f8 bishop, keeping Black's setup flexible.
catalan.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3: The Catalan: the bishop goes to g2 to press the long diagonal towards d5 and b7.
catalan.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 d5: Stakes the centre, entering the classic Catalan where the g2 bishop bears down on d5.
catalan.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 d5 Bg2: Aims through d5 at b7: whenever Black takes on c4 or moves the c-pawn, it grows stronger.
catalan.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 d5 Bg2 dxc4: Open Catalan: takes the pawn; White plays for lasting pressure on the long diagonal to win it back.
catalan.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 d5 Bg2 Be7: Closed Catalan: holds d5 solidly, freeing the game later with ...c5 or ...b6 and ...Bb7.
catalan.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 d5 Bg2 c6: Reinforces d5 so the long diagonal stays blocked, at the cost of a slightly passive setup.
catalan.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 Bb4+: Checks to swap the dark-squared bishops before White's queenside pressure builds.
catalan.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 c5: Strikes at d4 to open the position, choosing activity over solidity.
catalan.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3: Avoids the Nimzo-Indian pin and keeps g3 in reserve.

london.d4: Takes the centre with a pawn the queen already guards, so Black can't challenge it at once with ...e5.
london.d4 Nf6: Develops and stops e4, so White can't build a broad e4–d4 centre without preparing it first.
london.d4 d5: Matches White in the centre and stops e4, so White needs c4 to fight for the centre.
london.d4 Nf6 Bf4: The London: develops the dark-squared bishop before e3, so it isn't shut in behind the pawns.
london.d4 d5 Bf4: The London: develops the dark-squared bishop before e3, so it isn't shut in behind the pawns.
london.d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5: Hits d4 at once; with the c1 bishop gone, ...Qb6 can target b2.
london.d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3: Holds d4 and opens the f1 bishop, keeping the pyramid solid even if b2 comes under fire.
london.d4 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6: Attacks b2, which the bishop no longer defends, so White must spend a move on it.
london.d4 Nf6 Bf4 e6: Solid: prepares ...d5 or ...b6 and ...Bb7, keeping options open.
london.d4 Nf6 Bf4 g6: A King's Indian setup: the g7 bishop will fight White's bishop and the d4 pawn.
london.d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6: Develops and guards d5, waiting to see White's setup before using the c-pawn.
london.d4 d5 Bf4 Nf6 e3: Builds the d4–e3 pyramid behind the bishop, solid against any central break.
london.d4 d5 Bf4 Bf5: Mirrors White, getting the light bishop out before ...e6; c4 and Qb3 can then probe b7.
london.d4 d5 Bf4 c5: The sharpest reply: pressure on d4 and, after ...Qb6, on b2.
london.d4 Nf6 Nf3: A flexible start; Bf4 can follow while some sharper replies are avoided.

englishopening.c4: Controls d5 from the flank, keeping the centre fluid and leaving room for g3 and Bg2.
englishopening.c4 e5: A reversed Sicilian: Black takes the centre, and White plays the Sicilian a move up.
englishopening.c4 e5 Nc3: Adds control of d5, so Black's freeing ...d5 is harder to achieve.
englishopening.c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6: Develops and prepares ...d5, aiming to free Black's game in the centre.
englishopening.c4 e5 Nc3 Nc6: Symmetrical development, keeping e5 well supported.
englishopening.c4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 g3: Fianchetto: the g2 bishop rakes the long diagonal, pressing d5 and b7.
englishopening.c4 c5: Symmetrical English: Black copies, fighting for d4 so White can't take the centre.
englishopening.c4 Nf6: Flexible, delaying Black's choice of setup until White commits.
englishopening.c4 Nf6 Nc3: Develops towards d5 and e4, preparing e4 in some lines.
englishopening.c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6: Prepares ...d5; if White plays e4, e5 kicks the knight and the game turns sharp.
englishopening.c4 Nf6 Nc3 d5: Challenges d5 at once; after cxd5 Nxd5 it's a Grünfeld with colours reversed.
englishopening.c4 c6: Prepares ...d5 Caro-Kann style, so Black can recapture on d5 with a pawn.
englishopening.c4 e6: Prepares ...d5 with a solid Queen's Gambit structure.
englishopening.c4 f5: A Dutch setup: Black fights for e4 from the flank.

sicilian.e4: Grabs the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop, so White can develop fast and castle early.
sicilian.e4 c5: The Sicilian: fights for d4 from the side and unbalances the game, so both sides play to win.
sicilian.e4 c5 Nf3: Prepares d4 to open the centre while White is ahead in development.
sicilian.e4 c5 Nf3 d6: Controls e5 and prepares ...Nf6, keeping the Najdorf and Dragon available.
sicilian.e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6: Develops and adds pressure to d4, so d4 will be met by a quick exchange.
sicilian.e4 c5 Nf3 e6: Flexible: prepares ...d5 and keeps the f8 bishop's options open.
sicilian.e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4: Open Sicilian: opens the centre to use White's lead in development.
sicilian.e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4: Trades a wing pawn for a centre pawn, gaining the half-open c-file and a central majority.
sicilian.e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4: Centralises the knight with a lead in development; Black must now develop with tempo.
sicilian.e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6: Hits e4, so White must play Nc3 and can't set up the c4 bind.
sicilian.e4 c5 Nf3 d6 Bb5+: Moscow Variation: develops with check and trades pieces, sidestepping the main Open Sicilian.
sicilian.e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5: Rossolimo: pressures c6, planning Bxc6 to damage Black's pawns and avoid the Open Sicilian.
sicilian.e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 e5: Kicks the knight from d4 with tempo, accepting a weak d5 square for active pieces.
sicilian.e4 c5 c3: Alapin: prepares d4 so White can recapture with a pawn and keep a full centre.
sicilian.e4 c5 c3 Nf6: Hits e4 at once; after e5 Nd5 the knight is well placed and White's centre becomes a target.
sicilian.e4 c5 c3 d5: Opens the centre at once; the queen can recapture on d5 because c3 has ruled out Nc3.
sicilian.e4 c5 Nc3: Closed Sicilian: slow play with g3, Bg2 and often f4, aiming for a kingside attack.
sicilian.e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3: Smith-Morra Gambit: gives a pawn for fast development and open c- and d-files.

french.e4: Grabs the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop, so White can develop fast and castle early.
french.e4 e6: The French: prepares ...d5 with a pawn ready to recapture, at the cost of shutting in the c8 bishop.
french.e4 e6 d4: Takes the full centre; the French allows it, planning to strike at it with ...d5 and ...c5.
french.e4 e6 d4 d5: Challenges e4 at once, so White must decide how to handle the tension.
french.e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3: Defends e4 with a piece, keeping the tension while developing.
french.e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4: Winawer: pins the knight that defends e4, so the pressure on e4 becomes real.
french.e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6: Classical: attacks e4 again with a developing move.
french.e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5: Pins the knight that attacks e4, easing the pressure on White's centre.
french.e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 e5: Steinitz: gains space and kicks the knight, creating the locked French centre.
french.e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4: Rubinstein: releases the tension for easy development; solid, if a little passive.
french.e4 e6 d4 d5 e5: Advance: locks the centre and gains space; the fight becomes about attacking each pawn chain.
french.e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5: Hits the base of White's chain at d4, the key French plan; ...Nc6 and ...Qb6 add pressure.
french.e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2: Tarrasch: defends e4 while keeping c3 free for a pawn and avoiding the Winawer pin.
french.e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 c5: Strikes at d4 at once, often accepting an isolated pawn for active pieces.
french.e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5: Exchange: opens the position symmetrically, which frees Black's c8 bishop.
french.e4 e6 d3: A King's Indian Attack setup, sidestepping the main French lines for a slower game.

carokann.e4: Grabs the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop, so White can develop fast and castle early.
carokann.e4 c6: The Caro-Kann: prepares ...d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, so it can develop before ...e6.
carokann.e4 c6 d4: Takes the full centre; Black will challenge it at once with ...d5.
carokann.e4 c6 d4 d5: Strikes at e4, ready to recapture with the c-pawn to keep a pawn on d5.
carokann.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5: Advance: gains space and locks the centre.
carokann.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5: Develops the bishop outside the pawn chain before ...e6: the whole point of the Caro-Kann.
carokann.e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5: Hits d4 at once, spending a second move on the c-pawn for an open game.
carokann.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3: Defends e4 with a developing move, keeping the tension.
carokann.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4: Releases the tension, giving up the centre for easy development.
carokann.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5: Classical: develops with tempo on the knight; White often answers Ng3 and h4.
carokann.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nd7: Karpov: prepares ...Ngf6 so a trade on f6 is met by a knight, avoiding doubled pawns.
carokann.e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6: Offers a trade; after Nxf6 Black picks ...exf6 or ...gxf6 for an active, unbalanced game.
carokann.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5: Exchange: White aims for Bd3, c3 and a quick kingside build-up.
carokann.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5: Recaptures towards the centre, keeping a pawn on d5.
carokann.e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4: Panov Attack: hits d5, heading for isolated-pawn positions where White attacks.
carokann.e4 c6 d4 d5 f3: Fantasy Variation: backs e4 with a pawn to keep the centre, at some cost to the king's safety.
carokann.e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3: Two Knights: quick development, keeping the centre flexible.
carokann.e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg4: Pins the knight; Black often gives up the bishop for it to keep a solid centre.

pirc.e4: Grabs the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop, so White can develop fast and castle early.
pirc.e4 d6: The Pirc: lets White build a centre, planning to undermine it later with ...e5 or ...c5.
pirc.e4 d6 d4: Accepts the invitation to build a broad centre, which Black will try to undermine.
pirc.e4 d6 d4 Nf6: Develops with pressure on e4, so White must defend it.
pirc.e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3: Defends e4 with a developing move, keeping f4 and Be3 plans open.
pirc.e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6: Prepares the fianchetto: the g7 bishop will aim at White's centre.
pirc.e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4: Austrian Attack: a big pawn centre aiming for e5, the most aggressive try.
pirc.e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3: Prepares Qd2 and Bh6 to swap Black's key bishop, often with a kingside pawn storm.
pirc.e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Ng4: Hits the bishop before Qd2 and Bh6 can follow, winning time or the bishop pair.
pirc.e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Nf3: Classical: quiet development with Be2 and castling.
pirc.e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Bg5: Byrne Variation: harasses the knight and prepares Qd2, keeping Bh6 ideas.

modern.e4: Grabs the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop, so White can develop fast and castle early.
modern.e4 g6: The Modern: fianchetto first, keeping the knight flexible and inviting White to over-extend.
modern.e4 g6 d4: Takes the full centre, which the Modern invites so it can be attacked later.
modern.e4 g6 d4 Bg7: The bishop presses d4 down the long diagonal.
modern.e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nc3: Defends e4 with a developing move, keeping f4 or Be3 plans open.
modern.e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nc3 d6: Prepares ...e5 or ...c5 later, keeping a solid shell around the king.
modern.e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nc3 c6: Prepares ...d5 to challenge the centre directly.
modern.e4 g6 d4 Bg7 c4: Grabs more space for a bind that limits Black's counterplay.
modern.e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nf3: Calm development: White keeps a solid centre rather than over-extending.
modern.e4 g6 d4 Bg7 f4: A big pawn centre, threatening e5 to cramp Black.
modern.e4 g6 d4 d6: Delays ...Bg7 to keep queenside options like ...a6 and ...b5.

alekhine.e4: Grabs the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop, so White can develop fast and castle early.
alekhine.e4 Nf6: Alekhine's Defense: invites the e-pawn forward so it can be attacked later as an over-extended target.
alekhine.e4 Nf6 e5: Gains time on the knight and space in the centre.
alekhine.e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5: Centralises the knight, inviting more pawn advances.
alekhine.e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4: Builds the centre further, supporting e5.
alekhine.e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6: Hits e5 straight away, before White can support it.
alekhine.e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 Nf3: Modern Variation: supports e5 with a piece rather than more pawns.
alekhine.e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 Nf3 Bg4: Pins the knight that defends e5, increasing the pressure on White's centre.
alekhine.e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 c4: Kicks the knight again to gain space; with f4 it becomes the Four Pawns Attack.
alekhine.e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 c4: Chases the knight early, gaining queenside space.
alekhine.e4 Nf6 Nc3: Declines to chase the knight, steering for quieter positions where Black's provocation has no target.
alekhine.e4 Nf6 Nc3 d5: Challenges e4 directly; after exd5 Nxd5 Black develops easily.

scandinavian.e4: Grabs the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop, so White can develop fast and castle early.
scandinavian.e4 d5: The Scandinavian: challenges e4 at once, forcing an early decision.
scandinavian.e4 d5 exd5: Takes, so Black must spend time recapturing the pawn.
scandinavian.e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5: Recaptures with the queen, accepting it will be chased in return for easy development.
scandinavian.e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3: Develops with tempo on the queen, gaining time for White's development.
scandinavian.e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5: The queen sits on a5, pinning the c3 knight from afar and staying out of harm's way.
scandinavian.e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd6: The modern retreat: the queen eyes the centre and b4 while avoiding Bd2 pins.
scandinavian.e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd8: Retreats home: solid and safe, but slow.
scandinavian.e4 d5 exd5 Nf6: Delays the recapture to develop first, so the queen isn't chased.
scandinavian.e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4: Returns the pawn calmly for central space; Black regains it with ...Nxd5.
scandinavian.e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 c4: Holds the pawn; Black can gambit with ...c6 or ...e6 for development.

petrov.e4: Grabs the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop, so White can develop fast and castle early.
petrov.e4 e5: Matches White in the centre and frees the f8 bishop, so e4 doesn't control the middle on its own.
petrov.e4 e5 Nf3: Develops with a threat to e5, so Black spends the next move defending instead of choosing freely.
petrov.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6: Petrov: counterattacks e4 instead of defending e5, aiming for a solid, symmetrical game.
petrov.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5: Takes the pawn, so Black must win it back carefully: an immediate ...Nxe4 runs into Qe2.
petrov.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6: Kicks the knight first, so Black can take e4 next without the Qe2 trap.
petrov.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3: Retreats, letting Black regain the pawn; White aims to use a small lead in development.
petrov.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4: Regains the pawn in a symmetrical position, close to equality.
petrov.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nxf7: Cochrane Gambit: a piece for two pawns and an exposed king.
petrov.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4: Steinitz Attack: opens the centre to use White's lead in development.
petrov.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3: Defends e4 and heads for Four Knights-style positions.
petrov.e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4: Invites ...Nxe4, offering the e-pawn for quick play against f7.

philidor.e4: Grabs the centre and opens lines for the queen and bishop, so White can develop fast and castle early.
philidor.e4 e5: Matches White in the centre and frees the f8 bishop, so e4 doesn't control the middle on its own.
philidor.e4 e5 Nf3: Develops with a threat to e5, so Black spends the next move defending instead of choosing freely.
philidor.e4 e5 Nf3 d6: Philidor: defends e5 with a pawn; solid but passive, as it blocks the f8 bishop.
philidor.e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4: Challenges e5 at once, testing whether Black can hold it.
philidor.e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4: Gives up the centre for open lines and piece play, accepting less space.
philidor.e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nf6: Counterattacks e4, so if White takes on e5, Black takes back on e4.
philidor.e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3: Defends e4, keeping the pressure on e5.
philidor.e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 Nbd7: Lion setup: holds e5 with pieces, heading for ...Be7, ...O-O and ...c6.
philidor.e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nd7: Hanham: guards e5 with the knight, so dxe5 is met by ...dxe5 with nothing lost.
philidor.e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 f5: A counter-gambit hitting e4 at once: sharp, risky play for the initiative.
philidor.e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 e5: Reaches the Philidor through a Pirc move order, avoiding some of White's sharper options.

kingsindian.d4: Takes the centre with a pawn the queen already guards, so Black can't challenge it at once with ...e5.
kingsindian.d4 Nf6: Develops and stops e4, so White can't build a broad e4–d4 centre without preparing it first.
kingsindian.d4 Nf6 c4: Gains queenside space and hits d5, so a later ...d5 can be met by exchanging on d5.
kingsindian.d4 Nf6 c4 g6: King's Indian: concedes the centre now to strike it later with ...e5 or ...c5.
kingsindian.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3: Develops and supports e4, preparing a big pawn centre.
kingsindian.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7: The bishop eyes d4 down the long diagonal, the piece Black's whole plan relies on.
kingsindian.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4: Builds a big centre, gaining space but giving Black a target for ...e5 and ...c5.
kingsindian.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6: Prepares ...e5, and stops e5 from kicking the knight first.
kingsindian.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 Nf3: Flexible development, keeping e4 available next move.
kingsindian.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nf3: Keeps options open, often with g3 next, avoiding the sharpest King's Indian lines.
kingsindian.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nf3 Bg7 g3: Fianchetto: White's bishop meets Black's on the long diagonal, blunting ...e5 counterplay.
kingsindian.d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6: The King's Indian setup without c4, so White can choose a quieter system.
kingsindian.d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4: London-style: the bishop gets outside the pawn chain before e3, avoiding main-line theory.

nimzoindian.d4: Takes the centre with a pawn the queen already guards, so Black can't challenge it at once with ...e5.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6: Develops and stops e4, so White can't build a broad e4–d4 centre without preparing it first.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4: Gains queenside space and hits d5, so a later ...d5 can be met by exchanging on d5.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6: Prepares ...d5 or ...Bb4 and opens the f8 bishop, keeping Black's setup flexible.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3: Prepares e4, accepting that ...Bb4 can pin the knight.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4: Nimzo-Indian: pins the c3 knight to fight for e4, ready to give the bishop for doubled pawns.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2: Classical: recaptures on c3 with the queen, so White keeps a healthy pawn structure.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2 O-O: Castles, ready to strike with ...c5 or ...d5 once White commits.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2 c5: Hits d4 at once, using the queen's absence from d1.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2 d5: Claims the centre while White's queen is on c2, aiming for quick development.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3: Rubinstein: solid, preparing Bd3 and Ne2 so the knight can retake on c3.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3 O-O: Waits to see White's setup before committing the centre pawns.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3 b6: Fianchettoes so the b7 bishop joins the fight for e4.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3 c5: Pressures d4, so White must decide how to handle the centre.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 a3: Sämisch: forces the bishop to take, winning the bishop pair for doubled pawns.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 a3 Bxc3+: Doubles White's c-pawns, giving Black targets in return for the bishop pair.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 f3: Prepares e4 directly, taking the square the pinned knight can't control.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bg5: Leningrad: pins Black's knight in return, so the fight for e4 cuts both ways.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Nf3: Develops naturally, keeping e3 or g3 setups open.
nimzoindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 g3: Fianchetto, adding Catalan-style pressure on the long diagonal.

queensindian.d4: Takes the centre with a pawn the queen already guards, so Black can't challenge it at once with ...e5.
queensindian.d4 Nf6: Develops and stops e4, so White can't build a broad e4–d4 centre without preparing it first.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4: Gains queenside space and hits d5, so a later ...d5 can be met by exchanging on d5.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6: Prepares ...b6 or ...Bb4 and opens the f8 bishop, keeping Black's setup flexible.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3: Avoids the Nimzo-Indian pin, so Black needs another way to fight for e4.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6: Queen's Indian: the bishop will fight for e4 from b7.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 g3: Fianchetto, so White's bishop contests the long diagonal against b7.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 g3 Ba6: Hits c4, forcing an awkward defence like b3 or Qa4.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 g3 Bb7: Classical: aims at e4 and opposes White's g2 bishop on the long diagonal.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 a3: Petrosian: rules out ...Bb4 so Nc3 can follow without a pin.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 a3 Ba6: Pressures c4 straight away, so White must spend time defending it.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 e3: Quiet: prepares Bd3 to contest e4 from the other side.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 Nc3: Allows the ...Bb4 pin, heading for Nimzo-Indian ideas.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 Bf4: Puts the bishop outside the chain before e3, avoiding main-line theory.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 Bb4+: Bogo-Indian: a check to swap the dark-squared bishops or misplace White's pieces.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 Bb4+ Bd2: Blocks and offers the trade, so Black must decide about the bishop.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 Bb4+ Bd2 Qe7: Keeps the bishop for now and supports ...d6 and ...e5 if White trades on b4.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 Bb4+ Bd2 a5: Holds the bishop on b4, so after Bxb4 Black recaptures with the a-pawn.
queensindian.d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 Bb4+ Nbd2: Blocks with the knight to keep the bishop pair, at some cost in development.

grunfeld.d4: Takes the centre with a pawn the queen already guards, so Black can't challenge it at once with ...e5.
grunfeld.d4 Nf6: Develops and stops e4, so White can't build a broad e4–d4 centre without preparing it first.
grunfeld.d4 Nf6 c4: Gains queenside space and hits d5, so a later ...d5 can be met by exchanging on d5.
grunfeld.d4 Nf6 c4 g6: Prepares the fianchetto; ...d5 next turns it into a Grünfeld.
grunfeld.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3: Develops and supports e4, inviting the Grünfeld's ...d5.

grunfeld.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5: Recaptures, inviting e4, which gains time but gives Black a centre to attack.
grunfeld.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Nf3: Develops first, keeping the centre flexible.
grunfeld.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Bf4: Develops with pressure on c7, avoiding the main lines.
grunfeld.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Bg5: Develops actively, inviting ...Ne4 to hit the bishop and c3.
grunfeld.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Bg5 Ne4: Hits the bishop and c3 at once, gaining time.
grunfeld.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Qb3: Pressures d5 with the queen, aiming to win the centre.
grunfeld.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 Qb3 dxc4: Takes, gaining time when the queen recaptures.
grunfeld.d4 Nf6 c4 g6 g3 d5: A Grünfeld setup against the fianchetto, hitting the centre at once.

slav.d4: Takes the centre with a pawn the queen already guards, so Black can't challenge it at once with ...e5.
slav.d4 d5: Matches White in the centre and stops e4, so White needs c4 to fight for the centre.
slav.d4 d5 c4: Offers the c-pawn to lure Black's d-pawn from the centre; if ...dxc4, White regains it later with e3 and Bxc4.
slav.d4 d5 c4 c6: Slav: defends d5 while keeping the light-squared bishop free.
slav.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3: Develops and stops ...e5, limiting Black's freeing moves.
slav.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3: Adds pressure on d5, so Black must choose between ...dxc4 and holding.
slav.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4: Takes, planning ...Bf5 and ...e6 so the bishop is out before the pawn returns.
slav.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 a6: Chebanenko: prepares ...b5 to hold c4 or gain queenside space.
slav.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6: Semi-Slav: very solid, with ...dxc4 and ...b5 ideas.
slav.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3: Quiet: protects c4 and prepares Bd3, keeping a solid centre.
slav.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5: Gets the bishop out before ...e6 shuts it in: the point of the Slav.
slav.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bg4: Pins the knight, aiming to trade it to ease Black's position.
slav.d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5: Exchange Slav: a symmetrical structure that's hard for either side to unbalance.
slav.d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3: Allows ...dxc4, after which e4 builds a big centre.

benoni.d4: Takes the centre with a pawn the queen already guards, so Black can't challenge it at once with ...e5.
benoni.d4 Nf6: Develops and stops e4, so White can't build a broad e4–d4 centre without preparing it first.
benoni.d4 Nf6 c4: Gains queenside space and hits d5, so a later ...d5 can be met by exchanging on d5.
benoni.d4 Nf6 c4 c5: Benoni: challenges d4, inviting d5 to unbalance the pawn structure.
benoni.d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5: Gains space and cramps Black, avoiding a symmetrical centre.
benoni.d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6: Modern Benoni: opens the e-file and plans play with the queenside majority.
benoni.d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6 Nc3: Supports d5, so Black's exchange there leaves White a strong central pawn.
benoni.d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6 Nc3 exd5: Creates the Benoni structure: White gets a central majority, Black a queenside one.
benoni.d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5: Benko Gambit: gives a pawn for open a- and b-files against White's queenside.
benoni.d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5 cxb5: Accepts the pawn, so Black must prove the open files are worth it.
benoni.d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5 cxb5 a6: Opens the a- and b-files for Black's rooks.
benoni.d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e5: Czech Benoni: closes the centre for a slow, solid game.
benoni.d4 c5: Old Benoni: ...c5 straight away, inviting d5.
benoni.d4 c5 d5 e5: Closes the centre, aiming for kingside play with ...f5.

dutch.d4: Takes the centre with a pawn the queen already guards, so Black can't challenge it at once with ...e5.
dutch.d4 f5: Dutch: grabs e4 from the flank for kingside play, at some risk to Black's king.
dutch.d4 f5 c4: Gains space and prepares Nc3 to fight for e4.
dutch.d4 f5 c4 Nf6: Controls e4, the square the Dutch is built around.
dutch.d4 f5 c4 Nf6 g3: A fianchetto: the g2 bishop fights for e4 and the long diagonal.
dutch.d4 f5 c4 Nf6 g3 e6: Heads for Classical or Stonewall structures and opens the f8 bishop.
dutch.d4 f5 c4 Nf6 g3 e6 Bg2: The bishop presses e4 and the long diagonal towards b7.
dutch.d4 f5 c4 Nf6 g3 e6 Bg2 d5: Stonewall: holds e4 with pawns, accepting a hole on e5.
dutch.d4 f5 c4 Nf6 g3 e6 Bg2 Be7: Classical Dutch: flexible, ready for ...O-O and ...d6.
dutch.d4 f5 g3: Fianchetto first, aiming the bishop at e4.
dutch.d4 f5 g3 Nf6 Bg2 g6: Leningrad: a King's Indian-style setup that supports a later ...e5.
dutch.d4 f5 e4: Staunton Gambit: a pawn for fast development and attacking chances.
dutch.d4 f5 Bg5: Eyes e7 and provokes ...h6 and ...g5, loosening Black's kingside before ...Nf6 setups.
dutch.d4 f5 Nc3: Prepares e4 to break open the centre.
